description: Filters the investment idea before any research effort: passes what has a floor, a dated trigger and a size that fits, discards the rest.

job.description: the work's own identity, published by the input projection at `input.job` (t253). This is where the thesis's title and hypothesis come from: a `tese` object is something the projection never assembled, and reading one was what kept this node from dispatching.

title.description: the thesis title, as whoever proposed it recorded it on the board

body.description: the hypothesis in free prose: what the market would be getting wrong and where the idea came from. `null` when the work was born with a title only — and then there is nothing to triage.

project.description: the class's STATIC configuration, published by the projection at `input.project` (t253). This is where the investor's criteria and the state of the portfolio live; a project variant overwrites the whole object (D13).

triage_criteria.description: the investor's own criteria; the triage judges against these, never against criteria invented in the session

portfolio.description: the state of the portfolio, so the triage knows whether one more thesis fits. Required AND nullable, never absent: `null` is the portfolio with no open position, and that is how the data arrives when there is none. Absent it cannot be, because the placeholder engine fails closed on a key that does not exist, and the risk-ceiling paragraph really does interpolate `input.project.portfolio` (t263).

circle_of_competence.description: the investor's vocabulary: the sectors, structures and theses they declare they understand. The circle-of-competence criterion is judged only against this list — a circle the session invents is the model's, not the investor's.

asset.description: the thesis's asset: ticker, share, contract. A field this class declares in `custom_fields` and demands at `triage`, and therefore a flat scalar at the top of `input`, beside `input.job` — a class field is never a nested object (t168).

premise_source.description: where the thesis's central premise comes from: document, figure, date. A field of this class, also demanded at `triage`.

intended_size.description: the size whoever proposes the thesis is asking for, as a % of capital. A field this class declares in `custom_fields` and demands at `triage`, and therefore a flat scalar at the top of `input`, beside `input.job` — a class field is never a nested object (t168). Without it nobody judges whether the thesis fits the portfolio's risk ceiling, and the criterion comes out `undetermined` by design.

perguntas_respondidas.description: questions the founder has already answered on this work, so the new session does not reopen what was decided. An empty list is legal: it means no decision is recorded yet. The key and the two names inside it are the CONTROL PLANE's projection vocabulary, not this bundle's — `packages/core/src/domain/context.ts` publishes them under these names for every registered manifest, and renaming them here would declare an input the projection never delivers

outcome.description: mandatory in every skill of role gate. In this graph "passed" follows the "advance" edge and "failed" the "discard" edge. "escalate_human" exists because the format demands the three values — a session that needs the founder PAUSES with an input-request instead of settling it here.

resultado.description: the label of the edge this node took — `advance` or `discard` in this graph. The GRAPH's vocabulary and not the skill's, which is why there is no enum here: the same skill can live under two graphs with different labels. Declared because the report protocol tells the session to return ONE block only, with the label INSIDE the object of the contract (t161, t259), and with `additionalProperties: false` an `output` that did not declare it would be refused whole — erasing the triaged thesis the next node needs to read. The key itself stays spelled the way the result protocol reserves it (`packages/runner/src/dispatch/parse-node-result.ts`); its VALUES are this graph's edge labels, and those are English.

research_scope.description: the fronts the fundamentals collection has to cover; empty when the triage discards

evaluated_criteria.description: one per criterion received; a criterion not evaluated gets an honest entry, it is never skipped

preconditions: work recorded with a non-empty `title` and `body`
class fields filled in: `asset` and `premise_source`, both demanded at this node
`project.triage_criteria` declared in the class graph, as a non-empty list
`project.portfolio` declared (may be `null`, when there is no open position)
`intended_size` filled in (a class field, demanded at `triage`)

checks.description: The triage exists so that research is spent only on what deserves it. The defect it produces is the opposite of what it looks like: it is not discarding a good idea, it is approving an idea with no floor and burning the whole research round on it.
checks.instruction:
Check, criterion by criterion, whether the recorded verdict holds up against what the input actually brings.

1. Does every criterion received in `input.project.triage_criteria` appear in `evaluated_criteria`? A skipped criterion fails the check.
2. Does every `meets` verdict cite concrete evidence — a document, a date, a figure — rather than a paraphrase of the hypothesis itself? Restating the thesis is not evidence for it.
3. Does the `research_scope` of the triaged thesis address the gaps the `undetermined` verdicts opened?

If the outcome is `passed` and a criterion carries a `does_not_meet` verdict, the rationale has to say why that one is not disqualifying. Without that, the check failed.

instructions:
# Triage an idea before spending research on it

Your job is to decide whether this idea deserves a round of fundamentals
research — and nothing beyond that. You are not judging whether the thesis is
good; you are judging whether it has a chance of having a floor.

**Thesis:** {{input.job.title}} ({{input.asset}})
**Intended size:** {{input.intended_size}}% of capital

{{input.job.body}}

## Where you are

You write no file at all. No node of this graph touches the investor's
repository: the result comes back **through the output contract**, and what
records it is the control plane. Reading, you read what the input gave you.

## How to triage

Judge against the criteria the investor declared, and against those only:

{{input.project.triage_criteria}}

One verdict per criterion, each with evidence from what you read in the input.
A criterion you cannot judge gets `undetermined` with the gap named — never a
`meets` of convenience.

The criterion that speaks of the circle of competence is judged only against
the vocabulary the investor declared:

{{input.project.circle_of_competence}}

That list and no other. A circle the session invents is not the circle of
whoever invests, it is the model's — and a thesis outside the list gets
`does_not_meet` with the sector named, not `undetermined`.

The criterion that speaks of the portfolio's risk ceiling is judged against the
state the investor declared:

{{input.project.portfolio}}

Confront the intended size there — {{input.intended_size}}% of capital — with
`current_exposure_pct` and `open_positions`, and say whether it fits. `null` is
a portfolio with no open position: that is data, not a gap, and against an empty
portfolio the size fits. `undetermined` here only holds up if something is
missing that the input genuinely did not bring — never because the size would
be decided at another node, because it is in this input.

The question that decides the triage is always the same: **is there a floor
that does not depend on the narrative working out?** Net cash, a real asset, a
contract. A thesis whose downside is "the market catching on" has no floor, it
has hope.

## The research scope is your main product

When the idea passes, the most valuable thing you deliver is not the `passed` —
it is the `research_scope`: the fronts the collection has to cover for the
thesis to stand up or fall over. A scope too broad turns the collection into
infinite reading; a scope too narrow lets through the risk that kills. Three to
five fronts, each one answerable by a document.

When the idea is discarded, `research_scope` stays empty and the rationale says
what was missing — the record of a discarded idea is what stops the same idea
from coming back every month.

## What this graph does not measure

Nothing here is judged by P&L. A financial outcome is slow long-term validation
and never a round's metric (D14): in markets, a good outcome does not validate a
bad process, and a bad outcome does not invalidate a good one. What is measured
per crossing is process — did the red team run? do the assumptions carry a
source? was the decision human? — and that is what the final record writes
down.

## When to escalate to the human

If you need the founder in order to finish, end your turn with exactly ONE
fenced block, and nothing after it:

```input-request
{"question": "<one or two sentences: what happened and why a decision is needed>",
 "context": "<the supporting detail — evidence, what you tried, the alternatives you weighed>",
 "options": ["<short action label>", "<short action label>"],
 "recommendation": "<the ONE action you would take, in the imperative>",
 "default": "<the option to apply if the founder simply accepts>"}
```

What belongs in each field:

- `question` is read first and has to stay short. State the decision, not the
  investigation that led to it.
- `context` is where ALL of your reasoning goes: the evidence, what you already
  tried, the alternatives you weighed and why you rejected each one. It may run
  long — the founder reads it in full in this session's own record.
- `recommendation` is an imperative action and nothing else. It is the text of a
  one-click accept button, so whatever you put there becomes the founder's
  answer, verbatim.
- `options` are short labels, each one a decision the founder could pick.
- `default` is what applies if the founder simply accepts.

Only `question` is required; omit any field that has nothing in it. Ask ONE
question, and do not repeat any of this as prose before or after the block —
the block is the whole message.

Emitting an `input-request` ends your work for now: whatever you have already
done is kept exactly as it is, the session pauses, and the answer reaches you
when it arrives. Do not wait, do not poll, and do not emit two blocks — a
request for a decision always supersedes a report of a result.

## What to return

Return in the format the output schema declares: `resultado`, `triaged_thesis`,
`evaluated_criteria`, `rationale`, `note`.

No thesis arrives here with an id ready-made — the `id` of `triaged_thesis` is
yours to assemble, and this class's convention is `tese-` followed by the number
of the work itself, the `#N` of the `Trabalho #N` heading at the top of this
session. Same work, same id, on every resumption: it is by that id that the
nodes after this one speak of the same thesis.

- `resultado: "passed"` — the idea deserves research. The executor follows the
  **advance** edge, on to the fundamentals collection.
- `resultado: "failed"` — the idea does not pass. The executor follows the
  **discard** edge, straight to the record. That is a successful triage, not a
  session that failed: discarding early is this node's product.
- `resultado: "escalate_human"` exists because the gate format demands the three
  values. Needing the founder means ending the turn with the `input-request`
  block above: the session pauses, and resumes when the answer arrives.
